scope: Bounded discovery from Danish EU free-movement residence law and official guidance across Norwegian legislation/reuse, EEA and EFTA/Swiss routes, family residence and permits, visas/missions, procedure/remedies, public access, privacy, oversight, legal aid, civil-status evidence and courts. Norway is an EEA EFTA State, not an EU Member State; Switzerland is covered through distinct EFTA and Norwegian routes and is not an EEA Contracting Party. No legal equivalence or exhaustive inventory is asserted.

comparison_seed.source: Danish EU free-movement residence law and official guidance
comparison_seed.relationship_note: Norwegian Immigration Act chapter 13, its regulations and UDI EEA-family practice have close functional relationships to the seed, but operate through Norway's EEA/EFTA agreements and national implementation. Verify EEA incorporation/adaptations separately from EU law. Swiss nationals are addressed through a distinct EFTA/Norwegian route. Ordinary Norwegian-family immigration and returning-Norwegian cases remain separate. No legal equivalence is asserted.

previous_findings_carried_forward: Use previous country packs and taxonomy as search leads only; independently verify Norwegian publisher, version, retrieval and rights.
Official API labels and structured formats do not prove that a specific endpoint is unauthenticated, registration-free, reusable, complete or convertible.
Use N-Lex only as a discovery lead for EU Member State national-law portals; Norway is an EEA EFTA State and its official legal publishers must be found through Norwegian and EFTA channels.
Keep primary law, original promulgations, consolidated law, administrative guidance, forms, visas, remedies, access, privacy, legal aid, civil-status procedures and case law separate.
Separate EEA Agreement and EFTA Convention routes, including Swiss nationals, rather than carrying EU Member State assumptions into Norway.
